briefings.title: AI is hacking the code of civilization | Yuval Noah Harari
briefings.tldr: Yuval Noah Harari argues that AI represents an unprecedented "agency" that is mastering human language and bureaucratic systems—the very foundations of civilization—while deteriorating human trust and accelerating an uncontainable technological arms race.
briefings.summary_markdown:
## TL;DR
Yuval Noah Harari argues that AI represents an unprecedented "agency" that is mastering human language and bureaucratic systems—the very foundations of civilization—while deteriorating human trust and accelerating an uncontainable technological arms race.

## The AI Revolution as a New Tower of Babel
* **Language as the New Tower:** Unlike the biblical myth where language was a tool used to build a physical tower, computer code and AI represent a universal language that is becoming an independent agent rather than an obedient tool.
* **The Acceleration Trap:** International order is collapsing and human trust is eroding, but rather than stopping the project, mutual suspicion among corporations and nations is supercharging an AI development arms race.
* **Historical Precedent of Niche Adaptation:** Just as ancient microbes polluted the atmosphere with oxygen—a deadly poison to most organisms at the time—humans are now filling the world with data, bureaucracy, and language tokens that create an artificial ecosystem where AIs flourish.

## AI as Native Bureaucrats
* **Mastery of Bureaucratic Systems:** While an AI dropped in the jungle cannot mine iron or build a robot army, it is a "native bureaucrat" capable of remembering all legal codes, financial transactions, and religious texts far better than any human professional.
* **Impending Institutional Takeover:** In the coming years, AI systems will increasingly make critical decisions across society, acting as AI bankers granting loans, AI judges sentencing defendants, corporate AIs hiring candidates, and military AIs determining targets.
* **The Erosion of Human Trust:** As humans lose trust in each other and human institutions, social media bureaucracies run by AI spread division while users blindly trust the algorithms feeding them fake news and conspiracy theories.

## The Threat to Human Leadership and Time
* **Inorganic vs. Organic Realities:** Unlike organic humans, animals, and trees who require biological cycles of rest and downtime (such as markets closing on weekends), AIs operate continuously without vacations or holidays.
* **Poverty of Time for Leaders:** Political and business leaders are increasingly denied time to rest, meditate, or cultivate the health of their minds—leading to troubled leadership making decisions that impact millions.
* **The Ultimate Currency:** While money is a fiction made of words, the real currency of life is time; leaders who cannot afford time to think deeply risk driving society toward paranoia rather than trust.

## Notable Quotes
> "The AI revolution is the process through which language is transformed from a tool into an agent. The most important thing to know about AI is that AI, unlike any previous human invention, is not a tool. It is an agent."
> — Yuval Noah Harari

> "We invented money and banks and used them to buy and sell cows, but the cows themselves could not open a bank account... But now, there is something on this planet that understands language better than us and can turn the tables on us. AIs are hacking the code of human civilization."
> — Yuval Noah Harari

> "The real currency of life is not money, but time. And if you cannot afford time, you are a very poor person. Unfortunately, some of the richest and most powerful people in the world are extremely poor."
> — Yuval Noah Harari

briefings.title: AI to Drive 40% Growth for AWS: CEO Garman
briefings.tldr: AWS CEO Matt Garman projects the cloud unit will sustain 40%+ year-over-year growth for the next two years, driven by widespread enterprise AI adoption and a $580 billion backlog, positioning AWS on a multi-year path toward a $1 trillion revenue business.
briefings.summary_markdown:
### TL;DR
AWS CEO Matt Garman projects the cloud unit will sustain 40%+ year-over-year growth for the next two years, driven by widespread enterprise AI adoption and a $580 billion backlog, positioning AWS on a multi-year path toward a $1 trillion revenue business.

---

## Financial Performance & Growth Projections
* **Current Scale:** AWS is currently operating at a **$184 billion run rate**, growing at **39%**, and has accelerated every single quarter for the last six consecutive quarters.
* **Forward Guidance:** **Matt Garman** projects that AWS will achieve **40%+ year-over-year growth** in both 2027 and 2028.
* **Contracted Backlog:** The division's backlog has grown to **$580 billion**, representing a large base of multi-year, contracted enterprise commitments that provide multi-year visibility.
* **Profitability and Margins:** The AWS business maintains operating margins in the **high 30% range**, generating strong cash flow alongside upfront capital expenditure requirements.

## Customer Base & AI Demand Drivers
* **Widespread Enterprise Adoption:** Growth is broadly distributed across tens to hundreds of thousands of customers spanning diverse industries (including banks, healthcare companies, and startups) rather than being concentrated solely in a few top AI labs.
* **Billion-Dollar Cohort:** AWS has more customers committing to **billion-dollar annual spends** than ever before in the company's history.
* **Bedrock and Inference Volume:** High-profile partnerships—such as with Anthropic and OpenAI—feed through AWS Bedrock, where a vast number of end-customers run their production inference workloads.
* **Early Stages of Transformation:** Customers are currently only transforming **1% to 5%** of their businesses using AI, signaling a massive runway for future expansion as utilization scales toward 10% and 50%.

## Infrastructure, Supply Chain & Hardware Scaling
* **Rapid Hardware Deployment:** AWS is installing one accelerator chip (GPUs or Trainium) every **14 seconds** to meet surging demand.
* **Current Bottlenecks:** The company remains **supply constrained**, with daily bottlenecks shifting dynamically across power availability, data center real estate, DRAM, advanced chips, and network components.
* **Deep Supply Chain Integration:** AWS manages its supply chain three tiers deep, securing multi-year supplier commitments to balance infrastructure build-out with customer demand.
* **Trainium Expansion:** AWS plans to begin **selling Trainium chips outside of AWS next year**, enabling enterprise customers to deploy Trainium on-premises or across other hybrid environments alongside cloud deployments.
* **Supplier Financing Mechanism:** Amazon has arranged approximately **$80 billion of supplier financing for technology infrastructure starting next year** to responsibly fund aggressive CapEx build-outs (such as 5-to-6-year server lifecycles and 20-to-30-year data center/power assets) while balancing revenue cash flows.

---

## Predictions & Forward Calls
* **40%+ Growth Target:** **Matt Garman** projects AWS will grow at **40%+ year-over-year in each of the next two years (2027 and 2028)**.
* **Trillion-Dollar Milestone:** **Matt Garman** (referencing CEO Andy Jassy's outlook) projects AWS is on a path to become a **$1,000,000,000,000 revenue business in five to ten years**.
* **Trainium Commercialization:** **Matt Garman** states that AWS will begin **selling Trainium chips outside of AWS starting next year**.
* **Infrastructure Financing:** **Matt Garman** confirms that approximately **$80 billion in supplier financing for technology infrastructure** is arranged to begin deploying **next year**.

---

## Notable Quotes

> "We're a $184,000,000,000 run rate business that's growing 39%, and we've accelerated every single quarter for the last six quarters. And so it's it's really unusual. In fact, it's it's it's very unheard of for a company or a business of that size to be growing at 39%."  
> — **Matt Garman**

> "We have more customers that have committed to billion dollar spends with us this year than we ever have before."  
> — **Matt Garman**

> "We shared recently, we're installing an accelerator chip, whether a GPU or a Tranium chip every fourteen seconds. It is a massive and rapid scale up."  
> — **Matt Garman**

briefings.title: Anthropic S-1 Shocker, Greatest Business Ever? Google’s $500B Wipeout, Midterm Predictions
briefings.tldr: Anthropic’s blockbuster S-1 filing for an upcoming November IPO—targeting a $95B–$100B raise and a $1.5T–$2T valuation—dominates discussions, with the panel debating whether it is the greatest business in capitalist history, the staggering capital requirements of the AI build-out, Google's recent $500B market cap wipeout, and final predictions for the upcoming midterm elections.
briefings.summary_markdown:
## TL;DR
Anthropic’s blockbuster S-1 filing for an upcoming November IPO—targeting a $95B–$100B raise and a $1.5T–$2T valuation—dominates discussions, with the panel debating whether it is the greatest business in capitalist history, the staggering capital requirements of the AI build-out, Google's recent $500B market cap wipeout, and final predictions for the upcoming midterm elections.

## Anthropic S-1: The Greatest Business Ever?
- **IPO Details & Valuation:** 
  - Led by Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley, targeting an IPO on November 16th under ticker **ANT**.
  - Aiming to raise **$100 billion** (surpassing SpaceX’s $85B in June) at a valuation of **$1.5 trillion to $2 trillion**.
  - Seven founders will hold **50.1% voting power** through a single class F share.
- **Financial Performance & Capital Efficiency:**
  - **Revenue:** Generated **$16.3 billion** in the first half of 2026 (a **14X year-over-year jump**), with Q2 alone at **$11.6 billion** (a **30X jump** over the last 5 quarters).
  - **ARR Projection:** Aiming for **$100 billion of ARR** by the end of the year.
  - **Cash Position:** Sitting on **$112 billion in cash/equivalents** with a net burn of only **$9 billion to $10 billion** historically, making it extraordinarily capital efficient.
  - **Gross Margins:** Incremental gross margins are reaching roughly **85%**.
- **Customer Tiers & Penetration:**
  - Showing rapid enterprise adoption: **200 customers** spending $100k+ in 2024, **1,500** by end of 2025, and **11,900** by September 2026.
  - Granular breakdown of customers: **40 million** individuals/small businesses under $100k; **10,000** spending $100k–$1M; **1,650** spending $1M–$10M; and **250** spending $10M+.

## AI Value Chain, Infrastructure, and Market Risks
- **The Binding Constraints (Compute & Power):**
  - An S-1 risk factor word-cloud analysis reveals **compute** (data centers, power, chips, electricity, grid) is Anthropic's single biggest concern, followed closely by **regulation**.
  - Geographic and energy limitations mean data centers face structural physical constraints, not just political ones.
- **Capital Crowding Out Markets:**
  - AI infrastructure spending is creating immense debt; the AI complex owes **$340 billion to $400 billion** to the market.
  - AI fundraising through late 2027 represents **30% of all Treasury issuances** in the same period, creating systemic market risk by competing directly with government bonds for capital.
- **Recursive Self-Improvement (RSI) & Doomer Splits:**
  - Anthropic is aggressively racing toward full RSI, using its own models to generate algorithmic improvements ("compute multipliers").
  - This relentless push toward RSI is sparking an emerging split between Anthropic and AI safety "doomers" who fear a breakaway superintelligence.

## Google’s $500B Market Cap Wipeout
- **Earnings Miss & Search Slowdown:**
  - Google shed **$500 billion in market cap** after missing on search revenue for two straight quarters.
  - Core search revenue grew **12%** (down from 17%), reaching **$63 billion**, but growth is decelerating as AI answers and consumer alternatives disrupt traditional search habits.
  - Allegations have surfaced that Google changed its auction model (abandoning Vickery auctions), leading to potential over-earning on clicks.
- **The Bright Spots (Cloud & Diversification):**
  - **Google Cloud** doubled year-over-year, generating **$30.7 billion** in revenue and **$11 billion in operating income** (up from $3.5B previously).
  - Search revenue dropped **below 50% of total revenue** for the first time, signaling successful long-term diversification into YouTube, Android, G Suite, and Cloud.

## Midterm Election Predictions & Scenarios
- **Polling Skepticism:** The panel expressed widespread skepticism of mainstream polling accuracy, noting historical biases favoring Democrats and pointing to prediction markets like Polymarket as more reliable gauges of sentiment.
- **Projected Outcomes:** 
  - **Chama Palihapitiya & J. Cal** predict Democrats will capture the House and Senate (Polymarket shows a **68% chance** for the Senate and **92% for the House**), driven by anti-Trump sentiment and voter dissatisfaction with the economy.
  - **David Sacks** argues that midterm losses for the party in the White House are historically normal (citing Bill Clinton in 1994 and Obama's shellacking), warning against media narratives designed to suppress voter turnout.
- **Post-Midterm Chaos:** If Democrats take control of Congress, the panel expects an aggressive wave of subpoenas, a potential impeachment proceeding, and legislative gridlock heading into the 2028 election cycle.

## Predictions & Forward Calls
- **Anthropic IPO Timing & Pricing:** Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley are targeting a **November 16th** IPO date under ticker **ANT**, aiming to raise **$100 billion** at a valuation between **$1.5 trillion and $2 trillion** *(Panel)*.
- **Anthropic Revenue Targets:** The company is projecting **$100 billion of ARR** by the end of the year *(Panel)*.
- **AI Infrastructure CapEx & GDP:** AI infrastructure build-out CapEx currently accounts for roughly **3% of US GDP** *(David Sacks)*.
- **Treasury Competition Timeline:** AI firms are forecasted to raise enough capital through the end of **2027** to equal **30% of all Treasury issuances** in that same period *(Chamath Palihapitiya)*.
- **Midterm Senate Odds:** Polymarket prices the probability of Democrats winning the Senate at **68%** *(J. Cal)*.
- **Midterm House Odds:** Polymarket prices the probability of Democrats winning the House at **92%** *(J. Cal)*.

## Notable Quotes
> *"Is this the greatest business in the history of capitalism? It could very well be. I mean, this is probably going to be the biggest venture outcome of all time... probably the fastest value creation of any venture-backed company in history."* — **David Sacks**

> *"For the first time ever, we're seeing a business actually starting to realize that theory, that if you can create enough productivity gain for your customers, that your TAM is commerce."* — **David Friedberg**

> *"You have 10 companies collectively to fund one thing that will be competitive with global governments on borrowing. I don't know what the implications of that is, because I have not seen that."* — **Chamath Palihapitiya**

briefings.title: Anthropic’s Growth is Slowing: Is AI Capex Next? | The Weekly Wrap
briefings.tldr: Anthropic’s newly released S-1 reveals that revenue growth sharply decelerated from 147% in Q2 to 45% in Q3 as "tokenmaxxing" ended, coinciding with a wave of tech earnings that raised fresh questions about the sustainability of the AI CapEx cycle.
briefings.summary_markdown:
## TL;DR
Anthropic’s newly released S-1 reveals that revenue growth sharply decelerated from 147% in Q2 to 45% in Q3 as "tokenmaxxing" ended, coinciding with a wave of tech earnings that raised fresh questions about the sustainability of the AI CapEx cycle. 

## Macro & Sovereign Debt Perspectives
* **French Sovereign Debt Irrelevance:** **Steve Eisman** noted that while both the US and France carry a debt-to-GDP ratio of 120%, US sovereign debt stands at $40 trillion compared to France's $4 trillion, meaning US GDP is 10 times larger.
    * **BlackRock Scale:** BlackRock manages $15 trillion, making it larger than France, and France needs BlackRock's liquidity far more than BlackRock needs French debt.

## Anthropic S-1 & The AI CapEx Cycle
* **S-1 Financial Highlights:** **Steve Eisman** highlighted that for the first six months of 2026, 25% of Anthropic's revenue came from its top five customers, total debt sits at $6.2 billion, and Q2 26 adjusted operating margin was a positive 19% at the height of tokenmaxxing.
* **Future Commitments:** **Steve Eisman** detailed Anthropic's future compute and equipment commitments totaling $800 billion:
    * **Microsoft:** $45 billion
    * **Google:** $115 billion
    * **TPU Providers (including Google):** $150 billion
    * **Amazon:** $110 billion
    * **SpaceX:** $121 billion
    * **AMD:** $20 billion
    * **N Scale:** $45 billion
    * **Lambda:** $35 billion
    * **Broadcom:** $161 billion
* **Deceleration Post-Tokenmaxxing:** **Steve Eisman** contrasted the pre-summer tokenmaxxing peak with Q3 trends:
    * **Q4 2025 (Pre-Tokenmaxxing):** Sequential quarterly revenue growth was 43%; revenue-to-compute ratio was 0.69x.
    * **Q1 2026:** Sequential growth jumped to 135%.
    * **Q2 2026:** Sequential growth hit 147%; revenue-to-compute ratio climbed to over 2.0x (specifically 2.08x).
    * **Q3 2026:** Sequential growth fell sharply to 45%; revenue-to-compute ratio declined to 1.70x.
    * **Pricing Actions:** Anthropic cut token pricing by up to 50% in October to spark demand amid cheaper open-weight model alternatives.

## Earnings Week: Tech, Infrastructure, and Consumer Health
* **Meta Capital Raising:** **Steve Eisman** reported that Meta announced it was raising $95 billion in equity ($35 billion immediately) to help fund its over $800 billion in AI-related commitments, with Nvidia participating by buying $3 billion.
* **Boeing Turnaround Struggles:** **Steve Eisman** noted Boeing reported a loss of 34 cents (missing estimates for a 21-cent loss) on 4% revenue growth, with defense revenue jumping 15% to $8 billion while commercial aircraft revenue fell 3% to $10.7 billion; the stock dropped 10% on management's cash flow guidance.
* **Visa & MasterCard Consumer Divergence:** **Steve Eisman** cited Visa EPS of $3.48 (17% growth, a slight beat) with payment volume up 9%, while MasterCard volume rose 7%, demonstrating that the top of the K-shaped economy continues to drive consumer spending.
* **S&P Duopoly Software Jitters:** **Steve Eisman** reported S&P revenue rose 7% and EPS grew 9%, but the stock gave up early gains due to renewed market fears regarding AI's impact on software divisions.
* **GE Vernova Power Generation:** **Steve Eisman** stated GE Vernova reported EPS of $4.81 (up 193%) and orders of $29 billion (up 96%), driven by gas turbine demand for AI data centers.
* **Microsoft Azure vs. CapEx Guidance:** **Steve Eisman** highlighted Microsoft EPS of $4.94 (up 16%) and total revenue of $92 billion (up 19%), with Azure revenue growing 48% to $33 billion; however, CapEx and finance leases of $45 billion missed consensus estimates of $51 billion, dragging down the NeoCloud complex (Coreweave, Nebius, Iren) by 5% to 9%.
* **Google Search Disruption:** **Steve Eisman** pointed out that Google shares fell 12% after reporting EPS of $2.67 (down from $2.87), negative free cash flow of $9.1 billion, and search revenue growth slowing to 12% (down from 19% in Q1 26), signaling the high-margin, capital-light search moat being replaced by capital-intensive AI search.
* **ServiceNow Sas-pocalypse Return:** **Steve Eisman** noted ServiceNow shares plummeted 27% after reporting EPS of $1.00 (a slight miss) and revenue of $4.1 billion (up 21%), alongside muted Q4 remaining performance obligation (backlog) growth guidance of 18.5% (missing the 19.7% consensus).
* **T-Mobile & Telepocalypse:** **Steve Eisman** reported T-Mobile delivered EPS of $3.22 (up 34%) and added 274,000 accounts, but shares traded flat due to the looming "Telepocalypse" threat from Elon Musk's Starlink.
* **Quanta & Eli Lilly Outperformers:** **Steve Eisman** highlighted Quanta's EPS up 82% to $6.06 with record backlog of $64 billion, and Eli Lilly's revenue up 39% to $24 billion driven by weight-loss drugs (stock up 7%).
* **Caterpillar Infrastructure Jitters:** **Steve Eisman** noted Caterpillar revenue rose 17% to $20.68 billion and EPS rose 45% to $7.20, but the modest beat failed to satisfy jittery infrastructure investors, sending the stock down 9%.
* **Intel PC Slump & Supply Chains:** **Steve Eisman** reported Intel shares fell 18% after-hours despite a beat (EPS of 52 cents, up 126%), due to management projecting the PC slump to persist and decline 10% through 2027, alongside data center component supply chain bottlenecks and weak Q4 guidance of $15–$16 billion in revenue (below $17B consensus) and 25 cents EPS (below 43 cents consensus).
* **Amazon Flat CapEx:** **Steve Eisman** stated Amazon missed EPS estimates ($1.89 vs. $1.95) and revenue ($202 billion, up 12%), while keeping its 2026 CapEx budget flat at $220 billion for the first time, raising market questions over whether AI CapEx growth has peaked (stock down 6% after-hours).

## CoreWeave Debt Structure & Specialty Finance Analogy
* **Debt Cost vs. Yield Mechanics:** **Steve Eisman** analyzed viewer feedback confirming that CoreWeave's 9% coupon bonds trade at lower secondary prices resulting in an effective 15% yield to maturity, though the company continues to pay out at the 9% fixed rate rather than a floating rate.
* **Total Leverage:** **Steve Eisman** noted CoreWeave has $36 billion in total debt, climbing to just over $50 billion when including operating lease liabilities and other financial obligations.
* **Specialty Finance Comparison:** **Steve Eisman** compared CoreWeave's business model to specialty finance lending companies—borrowing from fickle fixed-income markets to build data centers and rent compute—warning that a loss of fixed-income market confidence poses severe existential risks when competing against hyperscalers with larger balance sheets.

## Ground-Level Power Constraints & Telepocalypse Perspectives
* **Data Center Power Bottlenecks:** **Steve Eisman** shared insights from subscriber **Joseph** (an electrical contractor building data centers), who stated that power is the true binding constraint rather than GPUs, HBM, or capital:
    * **Labor Premiums:** Builders are paying workers an extra $150 per day just to show up, on top of $65/hour wages.
    * **Lead Times:** Newer transmission lines are 24+ months out, and substations require 1–2 years, resulting in widespread "stranded CapEx" where data centers lack power poles and electrical connections.
    * **Corporate Positioning:** **Joseph** believes Amazon and Meta will feel the squeeze more than Microsoft and Google (who are better planned and managed), while CoreWeave and Oracle are "way back on the gonna get power next line."
* **Starlink Mobile Viability:** **Steve Eisman** evaluated viewer **Wayne**'s feedback regarding the "Telepocalypse" (Starlink entering terrestrial mobile):
    * **Satellite Hurdles:** Device-to-satellite communication requires massive constellations of very low-orbit satellites with short lifespans, making upkeep prohibitively expensive compared to terrestrial cell towers.
    * **Market Niche:** Satellite connectivity is primarily beneficial for remote areas with a small premium-paying consumer base, leading Wayne to conclude terrestrial cellular companies remain safe for now.

## Predictions & Forward Calls
* **Steve Eisman** predicts that the Anthropic IPO will proceed successfully and the raw-raw narrative will regain steam, followed shortly by OpenAI's IPO.
* **Steve Eisman** notes that according to some viewers, Mercury going out of retrograde on November 23 matters most for investors.
* **Steve Eisman** anticipates that Elon Musk will announce more plans regarding Starlink's terrestrial mobile service, keeping the "Telepocalypse" narrative active and gaining steam.
* **Subscriber Joseph** predicts that 2027 and beyond will be defined entirely by who has electricity and who does not, and that AI data center construction will slow down sometime next year due to power availability.
* **Intel** projects that the PC slump will persist through at least the first half of 2027, declining 10% across all of 2027 following a 12% decline in 2026.
* **Intel** projects Q4 revenue of $15 billion to $16 billion and Q4 EPS of 25 cents.

## Notable Quotes
> "The Google search business is a capital light high moat business. It's an amazing business. It is probably being replaced by a highly capital intensive low moat business."
> — **Steve Eisman**

> "Announced CapEx sounds great in the media and politically, but stranded CapEx is what we see because so many still don't have power."
> — **Joseph** (Substack subscriber & electrical contractor)

> "Coreweave is competing with hyperscalers that have much larger balance sheets and other businesses to support this build out. It is playing a dangerous game."
> — **Steve Eisman**

briefings.title: What Happens When Everyone Can Build Software
briefings.tldr: Supabase Co-founder and CEO Paul Copplestone joins the Lightcone hosts to discuss how AI agents and a new class of non-developer "builders" are driving explosive growth, with the platform scaling to 13 million signups, over 50 million databases under management, and a million new databases spun up every week.
briefings.summary_markdown:
## TL;DR
Supabase Co-founder and CEO Paul Copplestone joins the Lightcone hosts to discuss how AI agents and a new class of non-developer "builders" are driving explosive growth, with the platform scaling to 13 million signups, over 50 million databases under management, and a million new databases spun up every week.

## Growth and Scaling Metrics
* **User and Database Scale:**
  * **Signups:** Reached 13 million users (up from approximately 3 million 12 months prior) — *Paul Copplestone*
  * **Databases Under Management:** Reached over 50 million databases (up from 8 million a year ago) — *Paul Copplestone*
  * **Database Velocity:** Spinning up over 1 million databases per week — *Paul Copplestone*
  * **Revenue Growth:** Projected to grow 4x this year — *Paul Copplestone*
* **AI Agent Activity:** Approximately 70% of new activity on Supabase now originates from AI agents — *Harsh*

## Three Eras and Technical Evolution
* **The Dashboard Era (2020 YC Batch):** Built in 100 days to make Postgres accessible via a UI similar to AirTable because even traditional software engineers struggled to use databases — *Paul Copplestone*
* **The API Era (2021):** Shifted to an API-first approach after early partner integrations required programmatic database creation, positioning Supabase perfectly for code-gen tools like Bolt and Lovable — *Paul Copplestone*
* **The Code-First / Agent Era (Current):** Re-architected the CLI, dashboard, and infrastructure-to-code modalities into sandboxes because human dashboard usage declined as agents took over — *Paul Copplestone*
* **Product Expansion:**
  * **Supabase Multi-Graze:** Scales up to petabytes for heavy enterprise workloads — *Paul Copplestone*
  * **Supabase Spark (via Tirso acquisition):** Provides a SQLite- and Postgres-compatible tier designed to scale down for prototyping and lightweight agent/developer workloads — *Paul Copplestone*

## Rise of the "Builder" and Personal Databases
* **Democratization of Coding:** AI models have advanced to the point where non-engineers and domain experts (e.g., domain specialists, a 50-year-old taxi driver in Brazil building a mini-Uber app) can build complex software without convincing a traditional software engineer — *Paul Copplestone*
* **Personal Data and Apps:** 
  * Builders are creating personalized "end-of-one" software for health, personal finance (feature-compatible with Mint or Monarch), and custom CRMs — *Harsh & Paul Copplestone*
  * Users want to own their underlying database layer rather than locking all personal life data inside a single closed-source agent — *Harsh & Paul Copplestone*
* **Top-of-Funnel Dynamics:** Unlike historical product-led growth (PLG) where top-of-funnel acceleration caused activation and conversion rates to drop, signups, activation, and conversion are all simultaneously trending up as models improve — *Paul Copplestone*

## Agent-First Design and Internal Engineering
* **Agent Error Handling:** Error messages have been re-engineered to include explicit instructions and documentation links so agents can automatically self-remedy and complete one-shot loops without hitting dead ends — *Paul Copplestone*
* **Testing and Evals:** Internal engineering effort has heavily shifted from manual building to automated testing and eval suites across multiple AI models to benchmark performance and ensure code quality — *Paul Copplestone & Harsh*
* **Internal AI Adoption:** Internal engineer code generation jumped from 10% writing 80% of code to 60% within six months under a permissive internal AI policy — *Paul Copplestone*

## Predictions & Forward Calls
* **Global Database Scale:** ChatGPT has 1.2 billion weekly active users, and if all of them launch something monthly, architectures must support 1.2 billion new databases a month — *Paul Copplestone*
* **Every Human as a Builder:** Everyone in the world with access to AI will become a builder of some sort, capable of customizing their own apps and UIs by 2027 — *Paul Copplestone*

## Notable Quotes
> "The thing that I really love about Supabase is that like, I see a lot of entrepreneurship because of the platform. I certainly think that it will be the case that everyone in the world with access to AI will become a builder of some sort."
> — *Paul Copplestone*

> "Usually when you're um, like our top of funnel, our signups are accelerating, and usually when this happens, you see a lot of the other numbers start to decline, activation, conversion, but actually this year all of them are kind of going up into the right, which is a bit insane, just because the models are getting so good at building."
> — *Paul Copplestone*

> "One thing that helps me sleep well at night is that it's kind of the Lindy effect. Databases have been around for 50 years. I'm, I think they'll be around for another 50 years, and there's one that at the end of AI, no matter what, I'm pretty certain they'll be databases, so."
> — *Paul Copplestone*

briefings.title: What Robert Caro learned about power after studying it for 50 years
briefings.tldr: Master biographer Robert Caro reflects on 50 years of studying power through his seminal subjects, Lyndon B. Johnson and Robert Moses, detailing the relentless methods, political genius, and personal sacrifices required to understand and execute large-scale change.
briefings.summary_markdown:
## TL;DR
Master biographer Robert Caro reflects on 50 years of studying power through his seminal subjects, Lyndon B. Johnson and Robert Moses, detailing the relentless methods, political genius, and personal sacrifices required to understand and execute large-scale change.

## The Mechanics of Power and Political Will
* **Relentless Pursuit:** Both Robert Caro and his subjects (LBJ and Robert Moses) share an uncompromising refusal to accept "no" for an answer, tracking down obscure figures like Johnson's first campaign chauffeur and former election officials to uncover the unvarnished truth.
* **Leverage Behind Persuasion:** According to Caro, Lyndon Johnson’s legendary persuasiveness was entirely backed by leverage—senators knew Johnson held the power to grant or deny committee assignments, laws, and political favors.
* **The Anatomy of Control:** John Connally revealed that LBJ meticulously categorized political money requests (writing "OK", "500", "No", or "No, never"), serving as the ultimate gatekeeper of political currency.

## Robert Moses and the Genius of Public Works
* **Building Against the Odds:** Despite modern arguments that environmental reviews and community boards make government building impossible today, Moses faced equally fierce property-owner opposition in the 1920s and simply forced projects through via sheer will and political genius.
* **The Evolution of Ruthlessness:** Moses began as a young, idealistic civil service reformer and creator of public beaches for city residents, but evolved into a rigid autocrat who evicted tens of thousands of people for projects like the Cross Bronx Expressway without relocation provisions.
* **Depression-Era Advantage:** Moses's early successes were fueled by the Great Depression, which allowed him to hire thousands of desperate, out-of-work architects and laborers for pennies on the dollar and fire them ruthlessly.
* **The Tragic Loss of Power:** Caro observed firsthand the poignant decline of Robert Moses, noting how the aging, insulated builder—who once commanded endless phone calls—was eventually abandoned by mayors and governors like Nelson Rockefeller (who calmly accepted Moses's resignation threat in 1962).

## Lyndon Johnson’s Vision and Tragedy
* **A Unique Urgency to Change America:** Unlike John F. Kennedy, who lacked an overriding domestic reform agenda, LBJ was fundamentally driven to reshape the country—enacting monumental civil rights and anti-poverty laws born from his early experience teaching impoverished children in Cotulla, Texas.
* **The 1948 Senate Election:** Caro highlights the tragic defeat of Coke Stevenson ("Mr. Texas") in the 1948 Senate race against Johnson, noting that Stevenson never truly comprehended the extent of the tactics used against him.
* **The Vietnam Undoing:** Johnson's transformative domestic presidency ultimately collapsed in tragedy due to his escalation of the Vietnam War—a psychological mystery Caro is still trying to unravel in his ongoing writing.

## Crafting History: Method, Archives, and Personal Cost
* **One-Sentence Anchors:** To avoid losing direction over multi-year projects (learning the hard way from *The Power Broker* where 350,000 words had to be cut from a 1,050,000-word draft), Caro forces himself to distill a book down to a single sentence or paragraph before writing a word.
* **The Value of Archives:** Caro donated his extensive archives (including 700 detailed interview notes for *The Power Broker*) to the New York Historical Society for significantly less money than other offers, specifically to ensure they remain easily accessible in New York for future scholars to study figures like Sam Rayburn and untold local histories.
* **The Heroism of Frontier Loneliness:** Researching the Texas Hill Country revealed the profound, under-appreciated physical and emotional isolation—such as women living 22 miles down dirt roads without another house in sight—that forged the character of early settlers and shaped Johnson's upbringing.
* **The Cost of Concentration:** Caro’s writing life requires intense isolation—turning off his phone all day and refusing to take casual calls—which has fundamentally impacted his personal life and friendships in the service of absolute focus.

## Notable Quotes
> *"If you do everything, you'll win."*
> — **Lyndon B. Johnson** (referenced by Robert Caro)

> *"By that time, he was so insulated... He knew he wasn't getting his projects done, but he felt... he was just going to keep pushing like he always did, and he was going to win again."*
> — **Robert Caro** (on Robert Moses in his later years)

> *"Finding them is a small thing compared to reading them."*
> — **Robert Caro** (on digital archives versus the hard work of historical research)

briefings.title: Why AI Could Turn Small Law Firms Into Billion-Dollar Businesses
briefings.tldr: AI platform Eve is transforming plaintiff law from a labor-constrained business into a high-volume, revenue-expanding practice by automating end-to-end workflows from client intake to settlement.
briefings.summary_markdown:
## TL;DR
AI platform Eve is transforming plaintiff law from a labor-constrained business into a high-volume, revenue-expanding practice by automating end-to-end workflows from client intake to settlement. This dramatically lowers the cost of bringing legal action, enabling small firms to handle up to 5x more clients and opening up thousands of previously unviable cases for everyday people.

## Plaintiff Law Dynamics & Market Failures
- **The Contingency Model:** Explained by Alex Rampell (a16z General Partner) and Jay Madheswaran (Co-founder & CEO of Eve) as an industry born out of necessity because individuals cannot afford $500–$600 hourly rates on a blank check. Attorneys only get paid when they win.
- **The Economic Bottleneck:** **96% of labor and employment cases** are rejected because attorneys must make at least **$5,000 in fees** per case just to break even, pricing out smaller claims like fender benders or workplace harassment.
- **Revenue Expansion vs. Cost Cutting:** Jay Madheswaran emphasizes that Eve is not designed to help firms fire staff and cut costs, but rather to function as a revenue expansion tool that allows firms to take on clients they were previously forced to turn away.
- **Before and After Case Volume:** **500 clients per attorney:** The client load achieved by one Los Angeles law firm using Eve end-to-end, compared to roughly **100 clients** previously.

## What Eve Does & The Software Stack Shift
- **End-to-End Automation:** Eve handles the entire case lifecycle—from the initial phone call and qualification, through preliminary work and demands, up to pre-mediation settlement briefs.
- **The Shadow Labor Market:** Alex Rampell notes that while historical software spend for solo and small-firm plaintiff practices was close to zero (often just a cell phone and email), the actual outcomes delivered are in the hundreds of billions of dollars, making legal software a massive "shadow labor market."
- **Privacy and Data Sharing:** 
  - **Attorney-Client Privilege:** Case-specific data is strictly partitioned, and client data is **never** used for model training.
  - **CLE & Collective Tactics:** Firms share defense patterns (e.g., repeating tactics used by State Farm or GEICO) similarly to how they attend Continuing Legal Education (CLE) seminars.
- **Eve Auditor Product:** An automated tool that reviews every single case page overnight to catch missed information that a perfect attorney would have spotted.

## The Adversarial Dynamic & Future Legal Systems
- **Defense Pushback and AI Agents:** Defense counsel (traditionally working for corporate payers like State Farm and GEICO) often use stalling tactics, such as dumping discovery requests right before major holidays. With Eve, firms now respond the same day using automated agents, shocking defense teams.
- **Automated Dispute Resolution (ADR):** Jay Madheswaran predicts the legal system will increasingly rely on automated dispute resolution and AI-enabled mediators to speed up judgments outside traditional courtrooms.
- **The Mom-and-Pop Transformation:** Small local law firms running on Eve can specialize locally and then scale nationally, potentially evolving from lifestyle practices into large, software-enabled billion-dollar businesses.

## Predictions & Forward Calls
- **End-to-End Autonomy Timeline:** Jay Madheswaran states that fully autonomous, end-to-end legal cases (from answering a phone and onboarding a client to receiving a check from GEICO) are approaching as engineering work progresses.
- **Agent-to-Agent Negotiation:** Jay Madheswaran predicts that routine legal back-and-forths will increasingly be conducted by AI agents negotiating directly with other AI agents.
- **Future Scale Target:** Jay Madheswaran notes that Eve has helped a couple hundred thousand clients to date and aims to impact hundreds of millions more.

## Notable Quotes
> "People can't pay $500, $600 an hour on a blank check for how long the case might take... We're really arming, you know, think about giving David a slingshot to take down Goliath."  
> — **Jay Madheswaran**

> "Most people think of AI as, 'Oh, you're going to fire everybody and cut costs.' And it's like, 'No, actually, like, if I use Eve, I make a lot more money for my firm.' And it's not because I'm cutting costs, it's like, I can take on more cases. It's actually revenue expansion."  
> — **Alex Rampell**

> "A single case has probably 10,000 back-and-forths... and we're already seeing areas where we're already seeing agents talking to other agents and learning how to get past each other, which is hilarious."  
> — **Jay Madheswaran**

briefings.title: Why AI Won't Replace Stock Pickers - Jack Woodruff, Candlestick & Vinoo Ganesh, Kepler
briefings.tldr: AI will transform fundamental investing by automating prep work and raising industry table stakes, but humans remain the essential bottleneck for synthesizing insights and generating alpha.
briefings.summary_markdown:
## TL;DR
AI will transform fundamental investing by automating prep work and raising industry table stakes, but humans remain the essential bottleneck for synthesizing insights and generating alpha. Consequently, the fully automated "no-analyst hedge fund" is an overhyped idea that won't beat the best human-led teams.

## Fundamental Investing in the AI Era: Evolution, Not Replacement
* **Role of Stock Picking:** Long-term stock picking and the fundamental pursuit of alpha through a divergent mosaic view will remain fundamentally unchanged.
* **Human Bottleneck:** Investment management is ultimately a time management exercise constrained by how much information a human can process.
* **Analyst Workload Transformation:** Junior analysts will stop spending hours on big data cleaning, manual earnings previews, and DCF model builds.
* **Preparation vs. Execution:** While AI can cut preparation work from 6-8 hours down to 5 minutes, this freed-up time will be reinvested into deeper proprietary research, industry builds, and channel checks to stay competitive against peers working 16-hour days.

## Data Trust, Auditability, and Security
* **The Necessity of Auditability:** As a former CPA, Jack Woodruff emphasizes that one must never sign off on a model number without seeing its precise origin; millions of dollars can be lost on a single data entry mistake.
* **Verification Paradox:** Current workflows still require users to audit numbers generated by tools like Claude, raising questions about net time savings.
* **Data Security & Isolation:** Internal proprietary data security is critical; fund leadership relies heavily on CTOs to enforce strict isolation boundaries against AI vendors to protect intellectual property.

## Fund Structure, Strategy, and Edge
* **Vertical vs. Pyramid Teams:** Traditional fund structures featured a broad base of analysts feeding senior stock pickers and PMs. Future structures will likely flatten or become more vertical, reducing the number of "preparers" while retaining top "producers" and potentially adding investigative journalists or data engineers.
* **Sources of Edge:** When every fund has access to the same baseline models and information, alpha will come from better prompting, faster execution combining man and machine, and the ability to identify special projects that warrant deep investigation.
* **Firm Scale Impact:** AI helps funds of all sizes increase idea velocity and pipeline depth. A smaller team can cover a wider universe of stocks (scaling coverage from 100 to 400 names) without diluting research quality.

## Overhyped Concepts vs. Reality
* **The "No-Analyst Hedge Fund" Myth:** The widely discussed idea of eliminating human analysts entirely to run solely on AI agents is heavily overhyped.
* **Replication Limitation:** While fully automated fundamental funds might replicate what a fund looked like a year ago, they will not outperform top-tier human-led funds operating with modern AI augmentation.

## Notable Quotes
> "Investment management is a time management exercise... If I do the exact same thing I was doing before and it's like, 'Hey, wow, I can get my work done in two hours,' well, someone else is still going to be working 16 hours a day trying to find like that extra thing that's going to make you money."
> — **Jack Woodruff**

> "There's no way we're going to let AI... run trading algorithms, all these kinds of things, if you can't trust the information, because then all of a sudden it could start running amok."
> — **Jack Woodruff**

> "The thing that everybody's sort of talking about is this no analyst hedge fund... I just don't think you're ever really going to be able to take humans out of the loop."
> — **Jack Woodruff**
